verdict: Large correlated value overestimation on the current on-policy rollout distribution; no defect found in the specific SAC Bellman, entropy-density, terminal-mask or Polyak calculations checked.

implementation_checks.note: One update on an independent in-memory copy. No production checkpoint, replay, source or live process changed.

interpretation: The soft entropy term is negative, not a hidden positive return: its replay-next-state mean is -0.5834 reward units. It cannot explain positive Q against negative episode returns.

The critics match their own one-step bootstrap targets (mean Q93.29 versus target93.37; residual mean0.0765) and most replay terminal rewards (mean Q-19.65 versus -20). This does not validate their long-horizon predictions.

Both critics share almost all of the error. Their reset disagreement is0.897 compared with mean initial optimistic bias325.45. Changing the actor reduction from mean to min would lower reset Q by only0.449 and is not a sufficient correction.

Current actor samples receive3.715 more predicted Q than stored behavior actions at the same replay states. At discount0.995, persistent per-step approximation advantages can be amplified strongly through repeated off-policy bootstrap targets.

The replay is predominantly from older policies: current-policy log probability of stored actions averages-235.96, while sampled current rollouts average positive log probabilities. The standardized latent-action distance confirms action-distribution drift.

Actual current stochastic trajectories reached only1.594-1.766 retained radians before every episode dropped. The policy has learned a consistent partial rotation, but its favorable value predictions do not anticipate the subsequent loss.

CPU policy rollouts are current-checkpoint simulation measurements. They do not establish hardware performance or isolate every possible observation/model limitation. Twelve stochastic outcomes estimate expected Q with substantial return variance; each individual terminal return is exact.

bounded_next_experiment.name: Frozen-policy Monte Carlo critic calibration on the snapshotted40k actor
bounded_next_experiment.scope: Separate diagnostic branch under value_diagnosis; leave active bootstrap0004 unchanged.
bounded_next_experiment.data: Use stochastic rollouts0-7 for critic fitting and8-11 exclusively for held-out evaluation. Their NPZ files contain actual observations/actions and complete terminal soft returns.
bounded_next_experiment.procedure: Freeze actor and alpha at0.0333996862. Train only the twin critics against recorded soft Monte Carlo returns for at most2000 minibatches of256 using existing critic learning rate. Evaluate held-out initial Q bias and trajectory-wide errors every250 updates; save a separate diagnostic checkpoint only.
bounded_next_experiment.decision: If held-out initial Q becomes negative and absolute mean bias decreases by at least half without actor changes, the networks can represent calibrated returns and subsequent policy/data drift is the more likely driver. If calibration fails, investigate critic capacity/input scales and partial observability before another broad SAC run.
bounded_next_experiment.follow_on_if_calibration_succeeds: Test a new bootstrap branch with actual multi-step/Monte Carlo anchored critic targets and a10x slower actor, preserving the main paper method. Audit at5000 and10000 interactions; require the value bias to remain substantially below325 and retained-motion progress to exceed the current1.67rad baseline. Do not treat an actor mean-to-min change alone as the solution.
